correctness.rationale: All centered C4 balls are explicitly enumerated; the maximal ell^2 ratio is bounded by 81 Gram spectra. The embedded reproducible exact-rational program proves 79 uniform strict Sylvester certificates at 29/20, leaving exactly two alternating matrix choices. Their factored characteristic polynomial and exact positive eigenvector yield lambda=(7+2sqrt(10))/9>29/20. The eigenvector activates its radius choice strictly and attains equality, and spectral simplicity forces all extremizers. Complete finite-domain enumeration is exhaustive, not a sample. Assumes real counting-measure ell^2 and ordinary centered graph balls.

value.rationale: The 2014 founding finite-graph maximal-operator paper itself computes the C4 p=1 benchmark but not its p=2 norm; the first noncomplete cycle (also the smallest square/biclique) gives a structurally motivated missing sharp strong-type invariant. The complete exact classification of all nonzero extremizers proves that worst-case data must exhibit an alternating high/low pattern; the nontrivial irrational constant and strict separation from the other 79 radius choices are not a trivial interpolation or indicator computation. It offers a reproducible benchmark for spectral-radius selection methods on larger finite graphs.
